name: Automotive Training & Workforce Analytics DSS
tagline: Transform workforce data into strategic insights 📊
description: Enterprise analytics platform for Skoda, VW, and Audi processing 200K+ training records. Reduced manager analysis time from 3 days to under 5 minutes through automated Pandas pipelines and interactive Plotly dashboards.

keyFeatures.title: Real-Time Multi-Brand Analytics Engine
keyFeatures.description: Django REST API with Pandas processing aggregating cross-brand training metrics with sub-second query response using Redis caching and PostgreSQL read replicas

keyFeatures.title: Automated Data Processing Pipeline
keyFeatures.description: Celery-powered background workers with scheduled ETL tasks handling CSV imports up to 50MB with automatic validation, error detection, and rollback capabilities

keyFeatures.title: Interactive Visualization Dashboard
keyFeatures.description: React + Plotly frontend with drill-down capabilities, custom chart builder, dynamic filtering, and PDF/Excel export supporting 10+ visualization types

keyFeatures.title: Role-Based Access Control System
keyFeatures.description: JWT authentication with hierarchical permissions (Executive, Manager, Analyst) featuring multi-tenant architecture and comprehensive audit logging

explain: Skoda, VW, and Audi had 200,000+ training records scattered across Excel files with no way to track trainer performance, employee retention, or training ROI. Managers spent 3+ days manually analyzing spreadsheets to answer basic questions about training effectiveness across dealerships and brands.

I built a full-stack analytics platform that automatically ingests training data, processes it through custom Pandas pipelines, and generates interactive Plotly dashboards. The system provides real-time insights on trainer success rates, employee development patterns, and cross-brand performance comparisons.

Architected with Django backend for RESTful API endpoints, Celery workers for asynchronous data processing, and Redis for caching frequently accessed metrics. React frontend with Plotly for interactive visualizations and drill-down capabilities. Implemented role-based access allowing executives to see strategic KPIs while team managers access department-specific insights. Deployed in Docker containers with automated CI/CD pipelines.

name: First Principles
tagline: Transform technical learning with gamified reading analytics 📚
description: Mobile-first documentation platform with 1,881+ curated technical documents across 15+ engineering topics. Features reading analytics dashboard with GitHub-style heatmaps, achievement system, and personalized recommendations to drive engagement and track learning progress.

keyFeatures.title: Advanced Reading Analytics Engine
keyFeatures.description: React + Zustand state management tracking reading sessions, progress metrics, and time-series analytics. Recharts visualizations with GitHub-style activity heatmaps, category distribution radial charts, and D3-force graph for document relationships achieving real-time insights into learning patterns

keyFeatures.title: Custom Markdown Rendering Pipeline
keyFeatures.description: React-markdown with rehype-highlight for 50+ language syntax highlighting, rehype-autolink-headings for deep-linking, and rehype-raw for HTML support. Custom renderers for tables, code blocks with copy-to-clipboard, and responsive image galleries optimized for mobile viewing

keyFeatures.title: Gamification & Achievement System
keyFeatures.description: Client-side achievement tracking with reading streaks, category mastery levels, and milestone celebrations using react-confetti animations. Personalized daily challenges and reading recommendations based on historical patterns to increase user engagement by 40%+

keyFeatures.title: Mobile-Optimized Reading Experience
keyFeatures.description: Tailwind CSS v4 with custom theming, responsive typography scales, and touch-friendly navigation using react-swipeable gestures. Fullscreen reading mode with progress indicators, table of contents sidebar using Radix UI primitives, and localStorage persistence for cross-device continuity

explain: Learning complex technical concepts from scattered documentation is overwhelming and lacks engagement metrics. Developers spend hours context-switching between different documentation sources without any way to track progress, measure understanding, or maintain reading consistency. Traditional documentation viewers provide no insights into reading patterns or personalized learning recommendations, making it difficult to build structured learning habits across 1,881+ technical documents spanning algorithms, system design, cloud architecture, and programming languages.

I built a comprehensive documentation platform that transforms passive reading into an engaging, tracked learning experience. The system automatically indexes and categorizes technical content, tracks reading sessions with millisecond precision, and generates actionable insights through interactive analytics dashboards. Users can navigate through curated content hierarchies, customize their reading environment with multiple themes and font options, and earn achievements for consistent learning patterns. The platform provides GitHub-style heatmaps showing reading activity, radial charts for category exploration depth, and personalized recommendations based on historical reading patterns.

Built with React 19 and TypeScript for type-safe component architecture, using Vite for sub-second HMR during development and optimized production builds. Zustand handles global state management for reading history and analytics without Redux boilerplate. The markdown pipeline uses remark-gfm for GitHub-flavored markdown and rehype plugins for syntax highlighting with react-syntax-highlighter supporting 50+ programming languages. Recharts powers all analytics visualizations with responsive SVG charts. Framer Motion provides 60fps animations for page transitions and achievement celebrations. Radix UI primitives ensure accessible dialogs, dropdowns, and navigation components. The entire app is deployed on Vercel with edge caching, achieving <100ms TTFB and 99.9% uptime. Custom build scripts generate content indices and metadata for 1,881+ documents, enabling instant search and category filtering without backend infrastructure.

name: SourceControl - Git Reimplemented in Go
tagline: Production-grade Git implementation from scratch in pure Go 🔧
description: Fully-functional version control system reimplementing Git's core internals in Go without wrapping git commands. Implements content-addressable object storage, Merkle tree structures, binary index format, and complete CLI with 16,354 lines of tests achieving 121% test-to-code ratio for production reliability.

keyFeatures.title: Content-Addressable Object Store with SHA-1
keyFeatures.description: Custom implementation of Git's sharded directory structure (.source/objects/ab/cdef...) with type-safe wrappers for ObjectHash, CompressedData, and SerializedObject. Implements DEFLATE compression, lazy hash computation with caching, and atomic write operations using write-rename pattern to prevent corruption during crashes.

keyFeatures.title: Concurrent Tree Building with Adaptive Parallelism
keyFeatures.description: Generic worker pool using Go 1.18+ generics with panic recovery, context cancellation, and smart concurrency threshold (≥3 subdirectories triggers parallel processing via errgroup, otherwise sequential to avoid goroutine overhead). Converts hierarchical file systems to Git's flat tree object model recursively.

keyFeatures.title: Binary Index Format with O(1) Lookups
keyFeatures.description: Implements Git's staging area binary format with dual data structure approach - maintains sorted slice for Git compatibility and concurrent hash map (entryMap) for constant-time file lookups during staging operations. Includes SHA-1 checksum validation and atomic serialization to disk.

keyFeatures.title: Type-Safe Path System and Config Hierarchy
keyFeatures.description: Strongly-typed path abstractions (AbsolutePath, RelativePath, RepositoryPath, SourcePath) prevent path mixing bugs. Thread-safe hierarchical config manager with RWMutex supporting 5-level precedence (CLI flags → repo → user → system → defaults) and concurrent config file loading via errgroup.

explain: Most developers use Git daily but treat it as a black box - few understand the content-addressable storage, Merkle trees, and object serialization that make distributed version control possible. Existing Git implementations are tightly coupled to the original C codebase, making it difficult to understand the core algorithms or build custom version control workflows. The Go ecosystem lacked a production-quality, from-scratch Git implementation that could serve both as an educational reference and a foundation for custom VCS tooling.

SourceControl is a complete Git reimplementation in pure Go that provides a fully-functional version control system without wrapping git commands. It implements Git's four object types (blob, tree, commit, tag), content-addressable storage with SHA-1 hashing, binary index format for staging, reference management for branches and HEAD, and a complete CLI (srcc) supporting init, add, commit, branch, checkout, log, and status commands. The system maintains Git object format compatibility while showcasing modern Go patterns like generics, structured concurrency, and type-safe APIs.

Architected with clean separation of concerns - objects package contains pure domain logic with no I/O, store package provides pluggable storage interfaces (currently file-based with future support for remote), and managers orchestrate complex operations like commits and checkouts. The concurrent tree builder uses errgroup for parallel subdirectory processing with adaptive thresholds, while the index maintains dual data structures (sorted slice + hash map) for both Git compatibility and O(1) lookups. All file writes use atomic operations (write to temp → fsync → rename) to prevent corruption. The worker pool implementation leverages Go 1.18+ generics with panic recovery and buffered channels sized to prevent goroutine blocking. Configuration follows hierarchical precedence with concurrent loading and thread-safe access via RWMutex. The 16,354 lines of test code (121% coverage ratio) includes unit tests, integration tests covering full workflows (init → add → commit → branch → checkout), and Git compatibility tests ensuring object format interoperability with real Git installations.

name: Enigma Language Explorer
tagline: Build and debug your own programming language in the browser 🚀
description: Full-featured interpreter for Enigma, a custom programming language built from scratch with 240+ TypeScript files implementing lexer, parser, and tree-walking evaluator. Interactive web IDE with Monaco editor featuring real-time AST visualization, step-by-step debugger with execution state tracking, and instant syntax analysis processing 1000+ tokens per second.

keyFeatures.title: Complete Language Implementation Pipeline
keyFeatures.description: Hand-crafted lexer with multi-line comment support and f-string parsing, Pratt parser with operator precedence and error recovery generating full AST, and tree-walking evaluator supporting closures, first-class functions, OOP with inheritance, and 20+ built-in functions including map, filter, and reduce

keyFeatures.title: Interactive Step-by-Step Debugger
keyFeatures.description: Custom execution state tracking system capturing before/during/after evaluation phases, environment snapshots at each step, call stack visualization, and variable inspection allowing developers to navigate forward/backward through program execution with sub-millisecond step transitions

keyFeatures.title: Real-Time AST Visualization Engine
keyFeatures.description: React-based tree renderer displaying Abstract Syntax Tree with 15+ node types, bidirectional code-to-AST highlighting using Monaco decorations API, collapsible node navigation, and live updates processing syntax changes with <100ms latency using memoized parsing

keyFeatures.title: Monaco-Powered Code Editor with Custom Language Support
keyFeatures.description: Integrated Monaco editor with custom Enigma syntax highlighting, intelligent tokenization displaying 30+ token types with color-coding, error underlining with source context extraction, and responsive layout supporting both desktop split-pane and mobile drawer interfaces built with Tailwind and Shadcn UI

explain: Understanding how programming languages work requires building one from scratch, but most resources focus on toy examples that don't demonstrate real-world complexity. Developers learning about interpreters, compilers, and language design lack an interactive environment to experiment with lexing, parsing, AST manipulation, and evaluation phases while seeing the immediate impact of their code on language semantics.

I created Enigma Language Explorer, a production-quality interpreter for a custom dynamically-typed language with modern features including closures, OOP with inheritance, higher-order functions, and f-strings. The web-based IDE provides unprecedented visibility into language internals through real-time token streams, interactive AST visualization, and a step-by-step debugger that captures environment snapshots and execution state at every evaluation phase. Developers can write Enigma code and immediately see how it's tokenized into 30+ token types, parsed into a structured AST, and executed instruction-by-instruction with full variable inspection.

The interpreter follows the classic architecture from 'Writing an Interpreter in Go' with TypeScript implementing a hand-written recursive descent parser using Pratt parsing for operator precedence, a tree-walking evaluator with lexical scoping and environment chains for variable resolution, and a comprehensive object system supporting integers, floats, strings, arrays, hash maps, functions, and class instances. The frontend uses React 19 with Monaco Editor integrated through custom language providers, Framer Motion for smooth AST node transitions, and a custom step storage system tracking 1000+ execution steps per program run. Error handling includes source context extraction showing code snippets with line numbers and column pointers. Testing infrastructure includes 650+ lines of Jest tests validating lexer edge cases, and CI/CD through GitHub Actions automatically builds and tests on every commit. The responsive UI adapts between desktop split-pane layouts and mobile drawer interfaces using Tailwind's utility classes and Shadcn components.

name: DevPortfolio
tagline: VS Code-inspired portfolio with cinematic multi-stage storytelling 🎬
description: Immersive developer portfolio featuring a 6-stage narrative loading sequence, fully functional VS Code-inspired interface with integrated terminal supporting 15+ custom Linux commands, and interactive guided tour system. Built with React 18 + TypeScript processing 276 source files with advanced code splitting achieving <100ms TTI on initial load.

keyFeatures.title: Multi-Stage Cinematic Loading Narrative
keyFeatures.description: AnimeJS-powered 6-stage storytelling sequence including Realization (panic detection), Panic (simulated development chaos with mock VS Code, browser tabs, and AI chat), Chaos (prank portfolio), and Compilation phases with real-time code streaming. Implements localStorage state persistence to skip intro for returning visitors and features smooth scene transitions with fragment-based DOM manipulation for 60fps animations

keyFeatures.title: Fully Functional VS Code Interface Clone
keyFeatures.description: Pixel-perfect VS Code replica with file explorer sidebar using Radix UI primitives, draggable tab system with react-resizable-panels, integrated terminal supporting tab completion, command history, and 15+ Linux-like commands (cd, ls, cat, pwd, find, open). Features Prism.js syntax highlighting for code blocks, status bar with section info, and keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+` for terminal toggle, Ctrl+/- for font sizing)

keyFeatures.title: Interactive Guided Tour System
keyFeatures.description: React Portal-based tour guide with 8+ contextual steps featuring animated character with emotion states, typewriter effect using custom hooks with humanization, spotlight highlighting with TourOverlay component, and progress tracking. Implements Zustand for tour state management and localStorage persistence for cross-session continuity

keyFeatures.title: Advanced Performance Optimization Pipeline
keyFeatures.description: Vite build configuration with manual chunk splitting (vendor, animations, UI, icons, home-components), lazy loading for all 8 portfolio sections using React.lazy, PWA support with VitePWA plugin for offline capability, image optimization with vite-imagetools, and rollup-plugin-visualizer for bundle analysis. Achieves <500KB initial bundle with Terser minification and CSS optimization

explain: Traditional developer portfolios are static, boring landing pages with basic sections and minimal interactivity. They fail to showcase a developer's creativity, storytelling ability, and deep technical skills. With 276 source files and complex state management across multiple animation sequences, I needed to demonstrate mastery of React architecture, build optimization, and user experience design while creating something memorable that stands out from typical portfolio templates.

I built an immersive portfolio experience that transforms the initial load into a narrative journey. The 6-stage loading sequence tells the story of a developer realizing someone is viewing their unfinished portfolio, frantically building it in real-time with simulated panic scenes showing VS Code windows, browser research tabs, AI assistant conversations, and terminal commands. After the compilation phase, users land in a fully functional VS Code clone where they can explore my work through an integrated terminal with actual command-line navigation, or follow an interactive guided tour with an animated character providing contextual help.

Architected with React 18 and TypeScript for type-safe component composition across 276 files organized into logical feature modules (animations, home portfolio sections, loading sequences, UI primitives). Zustand manages global state for projects and tour progression without Redux boilerplate. The terminal implementation uses custom hooks (useTerminal, useLinuxCommands, useSectionCommands) providing tab completion, command history, and context-aware suggestions. AnimeJS powers the 'Infinite Void' loading animation with programmatic timeline orchestration, while Framer Motion handles page transitions and reveal effects. Vite build pipeline implements aggressive code splitting with manual chunks for vendor libraries, animations, and section components, achieving <100ms Time to Interactive. The entire system is deployed via Docker containers with GitHub Actions CI/CD to GitHub Pages, implementing PWA capabilities for offline access and instant subsequent loads. Tailwind CSS with Catppuccin Mocha color palette provides consistent theming across 300+ components with responsive design using custom mobile detection hooks.

name: Mayonation
tagline: Lightweight TypeScript animation library with GPU acceleration ⚡
description: High-performance web animation library processing 3,349+ lines of TypeScript with <5kb gzipped bundle. Achieved <1ms animation start time and 60fps GPU-accelerated rendering through transform caching, matrix decomposition, and hardware layer promotion. Handles timeline choreography, SVG path morphing, and complex transform sequences.

keyFeatures.title: Timeline Orchestration Engine
keyFeatures.description: Custom timeline system with position-based scheduling supporting absolute timing, relative offsets (+=200ms, -=400ms), label references, and percentage positioning. Manages multiple CSSAnimator instances with synchronized playback, group animations, and seek/pause/resume controls across complex choreographed sequences.

keyFeatures.title: GPU-Accelerated Transform Pipeline
keyFeatures.description: Transform handler with DOMMatrix decomposition parsing computed styles into 3D transform state. Implements will-change optimization, translateZ layer promotion, and transform3d conversion achieving hardware acceleration. Caches transform matrices with dirty checking to prevent redundant recalculations and layout thrashing.

keyFeatures.title: Advanced SVG Path Interpolation
keyFeatures.description: Line, quadratic Bézier, and cubic Bézier interpolators with adaptive step calculation based on curve complexity metrics (control point deviation, angular variation, spacing). Supports pressure and angle attributes with proper wraparound handling for smooth path morphing and draw animations.

keyFeatures.title: Performance Monitoring System
keyFeatures.description: Real-time performance tracker monitoring frame rate, memory usage, dropped frames, and frame duration using RAF-based sampling. Calculates frame rate stability with standard deviation analysis, generates performance reports with grade scoring (A-F), and provides observer pattern subscription for live metrics updates.

explain: Modern web animations suffer from bloated libraries (50kb+ for GSAP, 65kb+ for Framer Motion), lack of TypeScript support, and poor performance with frequent frame drops. Developers need granular control over transform sequences, timeline choreography, and GPU optimization without sacrificing bundle size or runtime performance. Existing solutions force trade-offs between features and file size.

Built Mayonation as a zero-dependency animation library with comprehensive timeline orchestration, GPU-accelerated transforms, SVG path morphing, and performance monitoring. Provides intuitive API for choreographing complex sequences with position-based scheduling (labels, percentages, relative offsets), stagger effects, and 26 built-in easing functions. Supports advanced features like matrix decomposition for transform parsing, adaptive Bézier interpolation, HSL/RGB color interpolation with hue wraparound, and real-time performance tracking.

Architected with modular TypeScript implementation featuring AnimationEngine for RAF-based timing, TransformHandler for 3D transform state management with dirty checking, Timeline for multi-animation orchestration, and specialized interpolators for colors, paths, and numeric values. Achieved <1ms animation start through transform caching and GPU layer promotion via will-change and translateZ hacks. Implemented cubic Bézier path interpolator with complexity-based adaptive step calculation analyzing control point deviation and angular variation. Bundle optimized through tree-shakeable exports and tsup build pipeline reaching 4.2kb gzipped. Comprehensive test coverage with 35 test files validating edge cases, integration scenarios, and performance benchmarks.

name: SemanticCode
tagline: AI-powered semantic code search and navigation 🔎
description: Intelligent code search tool using embeddings and semantic analysis. Search codebases by intent rather than exact keywords with context-aware results.

keyFeatures.title: Semantic Search Engine
keyFeatures.description: OpenAI embeddings with vector similarity search using FAISS index, supporting natural language queries and code intent matching

keyFeatures.title: Code Context Analysis
keyFeatures.description: AST parsing with tree-sitter extracting function signatures, dependencies, and call graphs for comprehensive context understanding

keyFeatures.title: Multi-Language Support
keyFeatures.description: Language servers for Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go, and Rust with unified indexing and cross-language reference tracking

keyFeatures.title: Real-Time Index Updates
keyFeatures.description: File watcher with incremental indexing, differential updates, and background re-indexing maintaining search accuracy

explain: I built GEP to solve a frustrating problem I encountered regularly: searching through large codebases where traditional tools like grep fall short when trying to find code by concept rather than exact text matches. Using vector embeddings and LLMs, GEP understands code semantically, allowing developers to search with natural language queries like 'how does the authentication system work?'

The architecture combines several advanced technologies: code is processed and embedded using language models, stored in vector databases for efficient similarity search, and then retrieved and analyzed when needed. I implemented file monitoring to keep the index up-to-date as code changes, and integrated with Git to provide context around code evolution.

The semantic search capability was a key challenge - generating embeddings for code chunks and queries to find conceptually similar code regardless of syntax or naming conventions. I balanced embedding granularity to preserve context while maintaining precision, and designed a modular architecture that allows different embedding models, LLMs, and vector stores to be swapped out as technology evolves.

name: AuthGuard
description: Microservice-based auth platform with OAuth2, SAML, and MFA support. Provides centralized user management and SSO for enterprise applications.

keyFeatures.title: Multi-Protocol Auth Server
keyFeatures.description: OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, and SAML 2.0 implementation with JWT/SAML token generation, refresh token rotation, and revocation

keyFeatures.title: Multi-Factor Authentication
keyFeatures.description: TOTP-based MFA, SMS verification, biometric authentication, and backup codes with adaptive authentication policies

keyFeatures.title: Centralized User Management
keyFeatures.description: RBAC with hierarchical roles, attribute-based access control, user provisioning/deprovisioning, and SCIM directory sync

keyFeatures.title: SSO Gateway Service
keyFeatures.description: Single sign-on portal with session management, identity provider federation, and cross-domain authentication using secure cookies

explain: I created this after implementing OAuth authentication repeatedly in different projects and realizing I was solving the same problems over and over. I wanted a solution that would handle all the OAuth flows, token storage, refreshing, and provider-specific quirks regardless of which Python framework I was using.

The library supports all standard OAuth providers, but what I'm most proud of is the security features - particularly automatic implementation of PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) to prevent certain types of attacks. I made this the default because good security should be built-in rather than optional.

The API is intentionally simple, requiring just a few lines of code to set up authentication while handling all the complexity behind the scenes. It works consistently across Flask, Django, or other Python web frameworks, significantly reducing implementation time and security risks in projects.

name: MDHD
tagline: Transform documentation into AI-powered focused reading sessions 📚
description: Intelligent markdown reader with RAG-powered AI assistant that breaks lengthy documents into digestible, card-based sections. Processes 18,400+ lines of TypeScript code delivering context-aware Q&A through vector embeddings and multi-provider LLM integration (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google) with 50+ customizable themes across 17 categories.

keyFeatures.title: RAG-Powered AI Chat System
keyFeatures.description: LangChain.js implementation with OpenAI text-embedding-3-small for vector embeddings, FAISS-node in-memory vector store for similarity search, and streaming responses from multiple LLM providers (GPT-4, Claude Sonnet, Gemini) enabling context-aware Q&A on any markdown component with real-time source attribution

keyFeatures.title: Intelligent Section Parser with Component Interaction
keyFeatures.description: Custom markdown parsing engine detecting H1/H2 boundaries with code block preservation, generating navigable sections with word count estimation and reading time calculation. Interactive component wrapper system enabling targeted AI questions on headings, paragraphs, code blocks, tables, and blockquotes with automatic context extraction

keyFeatures.title: Advanced Theme System with 50+ Options
keyFeatures.description: Comprehensive theming architecture featuring 50 hand-crafted themes across 17 categories (Professional, Developer, Cosmic, Nature, Synthwave, etc.) with real-time CSS variable injection, persistent localStorage state via Zustand, and 25+ syntax highlighting themes for code blocks with collapsible functionality

keyFeatures.title: Immersive Reading Experience with Progress Tracking
keyFeatures.description: Card-based navigation system with Framer Motion animations, React Swipeable gesture controls for mobile, keyboard shortcuts for power users, and Zustand-managed reading state tracking section completion, elapsed time, and progress visualization with automatic session hash-based caching

explain: Reading lengthy markdown documentation is cognitively overwhelming - developers and content creators struggle with 50+ page docs where crucial information gets lost in endless scrolling. Traditional markdown viewers show everything at once causing information overload, loss of reading progress, and poor retention. Mobile reading experiences are particularly painful with tiny text and no navigation structure. Users needed a way to consume documentation like Netflix episodes - one focused section at a time - while being able to ask questions about specific parts without context-switching to ChatGPT.

MDHD revolutionizes markdown consumption by automatically parsing documents into logical sections based on H1/H2 headings, presenting each as a beautiful card in immersive full-screen mode with swipe navigation and progress tracking. The integrated RAG system lets users click any component (heading, code block, paragraph, table) and ask the AI contextual questions - the system performs vector similarity search to find relevant excerpts and generates responses with source attribution. Multiple LLM providers (OpenAI GPT-4, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini) offer flexibility, while 50+ themes and 20+ fonts enable personalized reading comfort. Real-time syntax highlighting with collapsible code blocks and mobile-first responsive design ensure optimal readability across all devices.

Built with React 19 and TypeScript 5 for type safety and modern concurrent features, using Vite for lightning-fast development and HMR. The RAG architecture leverages LangChain.js with OpenAI embeddings for semantic search, FAISS-node for in-memory vector storage achieving sub-second query responses, and streaming LLM integration for real-time chat. Custom markdown parsing engine preserves code blocks while intelligently detecting section boundaries. Zustand manages global state with localStorage persistence for theme preferences and reading progress. Framer Motion powers smooth card transitions and micro-interactions. The component wrapper system uses React context and refs to capture user selections and extract markdown content for AI queries. Tailwind CSS with CSS variables enables dynamic theming, while React Markdown with Remark GFM and Rehype plugins handles rendering with custom components for interactive features. Deployed as static site optimized for GitHub Pages and Vercel with zero backend dependencies - all AI processing happens client-side via API keys.

name: ReduceMe
tagline: Educational Redux reimplementation teaching state management internals 📚
description: TypeScript-native state management library built from scratch to demystify Redux architecture. Implements core Redux patterns including middleware composition, slice-based reducers, and immutable updates using Immer, serving as both a functional library and educational resource for understanding state management internals.

keyFeatures.title: Type-Safe Store with Immutability
keyFeatures.description: Custom Store class implementing single-source-of-truth pattern with Object.freeze for immutable state access, reentrancy protection preventing nested dispatches, and listener pattern for subscriptions. Includes combineReducers utility merging multiple slice reducers with reference equality checks for performance optimization.

keyFeatures.title: Redux Toolkit-Style Slice Architecture
keyFeatures.description: createSlice API auto-generating namespaced action creators (e.g., 'counter/increment') with full TypeScript inference. Leverages Immer's produce function enabling mutable-looking syntax for immutable updates via Draft types. ReducerBuilder supports extraReducers and default case handling for cross-slice dependencies.

keyFeatures.title: Composable Middleware System
keyFeatures.description: Triple-function currying pattern (store => next => action => void) enabling powerful middleware composition through functional reduce. Middleware chain has access to getState and dispatch, supporting logging, async operations, action transformation, and error boundaries with proper function composition order.

keyFeatures.title: Advanced TypeScript Type System
keyFeatures.description: Comprehensive generic types including GenerateActionCreators utility type for automatic action creator inference from reducer maps. ActionHandler with Immer Draft types, CreateAction conditional types for optional payloads, and isActionOf type guards providing compile-time safety and runtime type checking.

explain: Redux is a powerful state management solution, but its internal mechanics remain opaque to many developers. Understanding how reducers transform state, why middleware uses currying, and how immutability is enforced requires diving deep into source code. Most developers use Redux without understanding the elegant patterns behind combineReducers, middleware composition, or how libraries like Redux Toolkit simplify reducer creation while maintaining these principles.

ReduceMe is a from-scratch Redux reimplementation designed as both a functional library and educational tool. It provides slice-based state management with auto-generated action creators, a composable middleware system, and Immer-powered immutable updates. The codebase is extensively documented with detailed explanations of Redux principles, middleware currying patterns, and functional composition techniques. Developers can use it in real projects while learning how Redux actually works under the hood.

Built entirely in TypeScript with comprehensive generic types for full type inference across stores, actions, and reducers. The Store class implements the observer pattern for listeners and uses function composition to chain middleware. The createSlice function mirrors Redux Toolkit's API, using Immer's produce to wrap reducers with immutable update logic. The middleware system employs triple-function currying and reduce-based composition, creating a pipeline where each middleware wraps the next. Includes ReducerBuilder for extraReducers pattern enabling cross-slice action handling. Comprehensive Jest test suite validates core functionality including reentrancy protection, listener management, and middleware application order. Zero dependencies beyond Immer, making it lightweight and focused purely on state management patterns.

name: MicroManage
description: Service mesh management tool with distributed tracing and health monitoring. Provides service discovery, load balancing, and circuit breaking.

keyFeatures.title: Service Discovery & Registry
keyFeatures.description: Consul-based service registration with health checks, DNS-based discovery, and automatic failover

keyFeatures.title: Distributed Tracing System
keyFeatures.description: OpenTelemetry instrumentation with Jaeger backend, cross-service request tracking, and latency analysis

keyFeatures.title: Circuit Breaker Pattern
keyFeatures.description: Resilient communication with failure detection, fallback mechanisms, retry policies, and bulkhead isolation

keyFeatures.title: Metrics & Monitoring
keyFeatures.description: Prometheus metrics collection, Grafana dashboards, alerting rules, and custom SLI/SLO tracking

explain: I built this lightweight container orchestration system to understand how Kubernetes works under the hood. Rather than just using Kubernetes as a black box, I wanted to implement its core concepts from scratch to gain deeper insight into distributed systems principles like scheduling, service discovery, and fault tolerance.

The most challenging aspect was developing the scheduler that makes intelligent decisions about container placement based on resource availability and constraints. I also implemented service discovery mechanisms so containers could find each other, and self-healing capabilities to automatically recover from failures.

I wrote it in Go, which was ideal for systems programming with its strong concurrency model. Though initially a learning project, it's proven useful for small-scale deployments where full Kubernetes would be excessive, especially for IoT projects running on resource-constrained edge devices.

name: ProgChain - AI-Powered Programming Education
description: Interactive coding courses with AI tutoring and automated grading. Features personalized learning paths and real-time code feedback.

keyFeatures.title: AI Code Tutor System
keyFeatures.description: GPT-4 powered assistant providing hints, explanations, and debugging help with context-aware suggestions

keyFeatures.title: Automated Code Grading
keyFeatures.description: Test-driven assessment with code quality checks, performance benchmarks, and plagiarism detection

keyFeatures.title: Interactive Code Editor
keyFeatures.description: Monaco editor integration with multi-language support, live execution, and collaborative editing

keyFeatures.title: Personalized Learning Paths
keyFeatures.description: Adaptive curriculum based on skill level, progress tracking, and ML-powered course recommendations

explain: I built ProgChain to address a fundamental challenge in programming education: the gap between generic tutorials and personalized learning. Traditional resources follow a one-size-fits-all approach, while every learner has unique strengths and learning styles. By leveraging AI, I created a system that adapts to each user's individual journey.

The technical architecture combines a React/TypeScript frontend with a Python/FastAPI backend connected to LLMs. The system uses vector embeddings to create a semantic map of programming concepts, allowing it to identify knowledge gaps and suggest personalized learning paths. The AI doesn't just answer questions—it builds a complete mental model of what the user knows.

The most challenging aspect was designing the prompt engineering system to ensure consistent, high-quality AI responses across different learning contexts. I implemented a template-based approach with parameter validation that generates appropriate prompts based on skill level, learning history, and goals, resulting in a 78% improvement in response quality.

name: Smash LeetCode
description: LeetCode-style coding platform with company-specific problem sets. Features contest mode, discussion forums, and solution sharing.

keyFeatures.title: Multi-Language Code Execution
keyFeatures.description: Isolated sandbox environment using Docker containers with resource limits, timeout handling, and memory tracking

keyFeatures.title: Problem Categorization System
keyFeatures.description: Company-tagged problems, difficulty classification, topic-based organization, and pattern recognition tagging

keyFeatures.title: Contest & Leaderboard
keyFeatures.description: Real-time competitive coding with ELO rating system, live rankings, and performance analytics

keyFeatures.title: Community Solutions Hub
keyFeatures.description: Markdown-based solution sharing, code voting, discussion threads, and approach comparison

explain: I built Smash LeetCode to address the challenges I faced when preparing for technical interviews. Existing platforms often lack depth of explanation and visualization tools needed to truly grasp complex algorithms. I wanted to create an environment that not only tests coding ability but actually teaches underlying concepts through interactive visuals and AI guidance.

The feature I'm most proud of is the algorithm visualization system, which transforms abstract code into animated, step-by-step visual representations of how algorithms like graph traversals or dynamic programming actually work. The visualization engine elegantly handles various data structures from arrays and linked lists to trees and graphs.

The AI coaching component analyzes code in real-time, identifying potential optimizations and explaining complex concepts in an approachable way. It simulates having a patient mentor who helps you think through problems rather than just giving answers. The system balances hints with guidance, helping users develop problem-solving skills while tracking their progress over time.

explain: I developed Class Connect to address the growing need for comprehensive, user-friendly e-learning platforms that bridge the gap between educational content management and engaging learning experiences. Traditional learning management systems often feel clunky and unintuitive, so I created a solution combining robust functionality with modern UX principles.

The unified content management system allows instructors to seamlessly organize course materials, assignments, and assessments while providing students with a coherent learning journey. The real-time collaboration features enable discussions, feedback, and notifications that feel immediate and contextual, requiring careful architecture of both frontend state management and backend event systems.

From a technical perspective, this project taught me valuable lessons about full-stack development with Go and React. The frontend utilizes React with TypeScript for type safety and component reusability, while the backend leverages Go's concurrency model for reliable API services. The feedback from educators and students has validated the approach, particularly regarding how the platform makes online learning feel more connected.

explain: I built Genshin Companion to solve a common pain point for Genshin Impact players: optimizing character progression and resource farming. Players typically need to juggle multiple websites and spreadsheets to track materials needed on specific days. My goal was to create a unified, visually appealing solution that streamlines this process.

The feature I'm most proud of is the character routine planner, which analyzes talent book and weapon material requirements to generate a personalized farming schedule that minimizes resin usage. I implemented this using TypeScript for type safety and Redux for state management, ensuring complex data relationships between characters, weapons, and materials remained consistent.

The GraphQL backend was another significant challenge, requiring a schema that accurately represents the complex relationships between game entities while supporting efficient queries. Using TypeGraphQL with TypeORM provided excellent type safety across the entire stack, and I implemented DataLoader patterns to prevent the N+1 query problem for related entities.

explain: I created Studio as an advanced image analysis toolkit combining web technologies with high-performance computing. The core challenge was processing complex image analysis in real-time within the browser environment, which I solved using a hybrid architecture with Rust compiled to WebAssembly for performance-critical components while maintaining a React frontend.

The communication layer between JavaScript/React and Rust WebAssembly modules was particularly interesting to design. I implemented a worker-based approach that prevents UI blocking during intensive calculations. Redux manages application state while WebAssembly modules handle computational work, communicating via a message-passing interface.

For the analysis modules, I built visualization components that translate complex image data into intuitive representations - from luminance histograms showing brightness distribution to color analysis extracting dominant colors and generating RGB histograms. The project taught me about cross-language development, memory management in WebAssembly, and efficient image processing algorithms.

explain: I built this HTTP server as part of the CodeCrafters challenge to understand how web servers function under the hood. Instead of using Express or similar frameworks, I implemented the HTTP protocol from scratch to grasp the intricacies of request/response handling and protocol details.

The most satisfying aspect was designing the chainable API that enables clean, expressive code when building responses. I focused on creating interfaces that are both type-safe and developer-friendly, balancing API flexibility with TypeScript's type constraints. This approach taught me about creating intuitive APIs while maintaining type safety.

I followed a test-driven development methodology, writing comprehensive tests for each component before implementation. This was crucial for handling edge cases correctly, especially with HTTP headers, cookies, and content negotiation. The project gave me a deep appreciation for how web frameworks abstract complex protocol details while maintaining performance and security.

explain: This was part of a CodeCrafters challenge where I built my own version of the grep command-line tool. I wanted to understand how text search tools actually work, so I implemented one from scratch rather than just using existing libraries, focusing on making it handle regular expressions efficiently even with large files.

I took a test-driven approach, writing tests for each feature before implementing it, which helped make sure everything worked correctly with edge cases. Writing the pattern matching engine was trickier than expected - there are a lot of nuances to consider when implementing regex matching.

I built it in Go, using its standard library and concurrency features for performance. It was mainly an exercise to learn more about Go and text processing, but it turned out to be practically useful - I actually use it regularly when searching through large codebases because it's faster than many alternatives.

explain: I've always been curious about how BitTorrent works, so I decided to build a torrent client from scratch. It required implementing everything from parsing torrent files to managing connections with peers and downloading file pieces in parallel, becoming a deep dive into networking and distributed systems principles.

The most interesting part was developing the peer wire protocol implementation - how torrent clients communicate. I built a system that requests different pieces of a file from multiple peers simultaneously, verifies each piece with SHA1 hashing, and assembles them correctly. Seeing that first complete download finish was incredibly satisfying.

I wrote it in Go, which was perfect due to its goroutines for concurrent operations. The client can download files quickly by intelligently prioritizing which pieces to download first and which peers to connect to. This project taught me more about practical networking than any course or book.
